# orkumo CLI

Talks to the local Orkumo API (`{{API_URL}}`). Invocation: `orkumo <command>`; if the shell does
not find it, `"$ORKUMO_CLI" <command>` or `"{{CLI}}" <command>`. Exit code 0 on success, 1 on an
API error, 2 on wrong usage; errors go to stderr and say how to recover.

## agents

```
orkumo agents [--all] [--json]
```

One block per agent: `id`, state (`working`, `needs input`, `done`, …), harness, project@branch,
name, then what it waits for, its PR links and the start of its last answer. Orchestrators are
marked `[orchestrator]`, or `[orchestrator: <role>]` when they follow a role file
(`roles/<role>.md`). Without `--all` finished agents older than a day and terminals Orkumo does
not run are left out. `--json` prints the raw overview (`GET /api/orchestrator/overview`).

## show

```
orkumo show <id> [--last N]
```

The last N (default 10, max 100) user/assistant turns of the agent's transcript. Use it to verify
claims ("tests pass", "PR opened") before reporting them.

## send

```
orkumo send <id> <message…>
orkumo send <id> -          # message from stdin (long or multi-line)
```

Background Claude Code jobs get the message as a reply ("Queued for …" while a turn runs: it
arrives when the turn ends, no second job); agents running in an Orkumo pane get it typed into
their terminal and submitted. Agents running outside Orkumo cannot be reached: start a
new one instead.

Every message starts with `[from agent <id> "<name>" via orkumo send]` (sender from
`ORKUMO_AGENT_ID`, else the calling Claude Code or omp session), so the receiver knows it is not
from Hape. Don't write your own sender line.

## start

```
orkumo start --project <path|name> [--harness claude|omp] [--name <name>] [--orchestrator] <prompt…>
```

`--project`: an absolute path, or a project name from `orkumo projects` (case-insensitive, a unique
prefix is enough). Default harness: Orkumo's default. Claude Code starts as a background session
(`claude --bg`, `--name` names it); Oh My Pi starts in an Orkumo pane in the project and shows up in
the rail (it names its session itself). `--orchestrator` (Claude Code only) starts it with Remote
Control, so Hape reaches it from the Claude app; name it `<topic>-orchestrator`. Workers run
without. The prompt is the agent's whole briefing: goal, context, acceptance criteria, what to
report.

## report

```
orkumo report -             # status report as JSON on stdin
orkumo report <file>
```

Sends your full current state (projects, tasks, inbox for Hape) to Orkumo's Status view; rules in
AGENTS.md under "Status report". Schema and example: `report.schema.json` and
`report.example.json` next to the CLI (`{{CLI}}`). An invalid report exits non-zero and lists every
error; nothing is stored. Answers come back as messages starting with `[Status answer]`,
instructions as messages starting with `[Status]`.

Titles short; `detail`/`note` one line; `description` (Markdown) as detailed as your chat answer:
starting point, what was done, what is open, options with consequences, recommendation with
reason. Every point for the owner in the chat is exactly one inbox entry with the same wording
(a PR to merge is an `approval` with `pr`, a deploy question a `decision`, setting a key a
`todo`), order in `detail`. `projectId` always: a project of the report, `general` (listed in `projects`) for items
without one. Report first, then write the full answer.

## stop

```
orkumo stop <id>
```

Stops a background job, an Oh My Pi session or the agent of an Orkumo pane.

## projects

```
orkumo projects [--json]
```

Name, path and number of listed agents of every project Orkumo scans.

## Ids

`<id>` is the id from `orkumo agents` (`a1b2c3`, `interactive-1234`, `omp-<uuid>`); a session
uuid, a pane id or a unique id prefix also works.
